mainTopic: When a mat (מחצלת) may be used as סכך: the dispute over a plain mat, a ברייתא on mat types, and the טומאה of חוצלות.
overview: The amud asks when a reed mat (מחצלת) may be used as סכך. A mat made for lying on can become טמא, so it is invalid, while a mat made for roofing is valid. The question is a plain mat (סתם) made with no stated purpose. רבא first reads the משנה so that רבי אליעזר is lenient about a plain small mat. אביי rejects this from רבי אליעזר's word order and from a ברייתא. רב פפא then explains that everyone agrees a plain small mat is for lying, and the dispute is only about a plain large mat: the תנא קמא says it is for roofing, and רבי אליעזר says it is also for lying. Next, a ברייתא sorts mats by material and weave, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי and רבי דוסא allow them all. The גמרא then brings a משנה where רבי דוסא and the חכמים argue about the טומאה of חוצלות, rereads the חכמים as saying 'even מדרס', and asks what חוצלות are. ריש לקיש says they are actual mats, which fits a tradition of רבי חייא and his sons about the mats of אושא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's reading: a plain large mat counts as made for roofing
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה forbids a large mat only when it was made for lying on. This implies that a plain (סתם) large mat is treated as made for roofing and may be used as סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what the משנה is saying: A large reed mat that someone made for lying on can become impure, and you may not roof a סוכה with it. The reason is only because he made it for lying. But a plain one, made with no stated purpose, is treated as if he made it for roofing, and you may roof with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is continuing his explanation of the משנה. He is reading the משנה's words in a way that fixes an earlier difficulty in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key move is a 'טעמא' inference: the משנה only forbids the mat because it was made for lying. So if it was made with no purpose (סתם), the default for a large mat is roofing. A large mat is usually made to cover things, not to sleep on.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [the source] means. Used to reread a text.
Lying down (a mat used as bedding)
Plain, unspecified; made with no stated purpose
Can become ritually impure (so it is a כלי and invalid as סכך)

steps.confusionAlert: Being able to become טמא is the reason a mat cannot be used as סכך. A mat for lying on is a utensil and can become טמא, so it is invalid. A mat for roofing is not a utensil, so it is fine.

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
A large mat of reeds,
if he made it for lying on —
it can become impure, and one may not roof with it.
The reason is that he made it for lying on,
but a plain one —
is treated as if he made it for roofing,
and one may roof with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's resolution on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה through a 'טעמא' inference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to have no clear default for a plain mat
steps.terutzMaskana: A plain large mat is treated as made for roofing and is valid as סכך

steps.title: רבא's reading: a plain small mat counts as made for lying
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: a small mat is allowed only if it was made for roofing. This implies that a plain small mat is treated as made for lying on and is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A small mat that someone made for roofing may be used to roof a סוכה. The reason is only because he made it for roofing. But a plain one is treated as if he made it for lying on, and you may not roof with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies the same kind of inference to the small mat. This time the result is the opposite of the large mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small mat is usually used for sleeping or sitting. So when no purpose is stated, the default is 'for lying', and it cannot be used as סכך. In רבא's reading, the תנא קמא gives the two sizes opposite defaults.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason; introduces an inference from the exact wording
It is treated as if he made it [for that purpose]

phrases.english: (A small one, if he made it for roofing —
one may roof with it.
The reason is that he made it for roofing,
but a plain one —
is treated as if he made it for lying on,
and one may not roof with it.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבא's reading, applied to the small mat
steps.terutzMaskana: For the תנא קמא, a plain small mat is for lying and is invalid

steps.title: רבא's reading of רבי אליעזר: any plain mat is valid
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, רבי אליעזר argues on the small mat. He holds that both small and large plain mats are valid as סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר comes to say: whether small or large, a plain mat is valid for roofing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his reading by explaining what רבי אליעזר adds. In this reading, רבי אליעזר is more lenient than the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading, the two opinions disagree only about a plain small mat. The תנא קמא says it is for lying and invalid. רבי אליעזר says it is valid, just like a large one.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's picture: the תנא קמא says a plain large mat is valid and a plain small mat is invalid. רבי אליעזר is lenient and says both are valid.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer comes to say:
both a small one and a large one,
if plain — are valid for roofing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's reading by placing רבי אליעזר in it
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about a plain small mat, and רבי אליעזר is lenient

steps.title: אביי's challenge from the word order
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that if the dispute is only about the small mat, רבי אליעזר should have said 'large and small', not 'small and large'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, when רבי אליעזר says 'both a small one and a large one', he should have said 'both a large one and a small one'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's reading by looking at how רבי אליעזר's words are ordered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a 'both X and Y' phrase, you normally say the obvious case first and then add the new case. If the large mat was never in question and the new point is the small mat, the order should be 'large and small'. Since רבי אליעזר says 'small and large', it sounds like the new point is the large mat.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If so,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
'both a small one and a large one' —
'both a large one and a small one'
he should have said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the dispute is about the small mat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word order suggests that the large mat is the new point under dispute

steps.title: אביי's second challenge: a ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר is stricter
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a ברייתא showing that the dispute is about the large mat, and that רבי אליעזר is the strict one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: when they argue, it is about the large mat, and רבי אליעזר is the strict one. As a ברייתא teaches: You may roof with a large reed mat. רבי אליעזר says: Only if it cannot become impure may you roof with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second, stronger objection, backed by a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's תנא קמא allows a large mat with no conditions. רבי אליעזר adds a condition: only if it cannot become טמא. That means a plain large mat might be for lying, so רבי אליעזר is stricter. This is the opposite of רבא's lenient רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; introduces an additional challenge

phrases.english: And furthermore:
when they disagree, it is about the large one that they disagree —
and Rabbi Eliezer is stringent.
As it is taught in a Baraita:
A large reed mat — one may roof with it.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it cannot become impure —
one may roof with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, בִּגְדוֹלָה הוּא דִּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, added to אביי's first one
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי אליעזר is lenient about the small mat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows the dispute is about the large mat, with רבי אליעזר on the strict side

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone agrees a plain small mat is for lying
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא drops רבא's reading. He says there is no dispute about the small mat: a plain one is for lying and is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: About a small mat, everyone agrees that a plain one is for lying on.
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' signals that רבא's approach is rejected. רב פפא starts a new explanation of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers אביי's challenges by removing the small mat from the argument completely. Both opinions agree that a plain small mat is for lying.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the earlier approach is dropped

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Regarding a small one, everyone agrees
that a plain one is for lying on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא: the dispute was about the small mat
steps.terutzMaskana: No dispute about the small mat: a plain small mat is for lying

steps.title: רב פפא: the real dispute is about a plain large mat
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that a plain large mat is for roofing. רבי אליעזר holds that it too is for lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about a large mat. The תנא קמא holds a plain large mat is for roofing. רבי אליעזר holds a plain large mat is also for lying on.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his explanation by placing the argument on the large mat. This fits both of אביי's objections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי אליעזר is the strict one, which matches the ברייתא. The order 'small and large' also fits: he starts with the agreed case (small) and adds the disputed case (large).

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture (רב פפא): a plain small mat is for lying, according to everyone. For a plain large mat, the תנא קמא says it is for roofing (valid), and רבי אליעזר says it is for lying (invalid).
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles how 'סתם' (no stated purpose) is judged for each mat size. That decides whether a plain mat is valid סכך.

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is about a large one:
the first Tanna holds:
a plain large one is for roofing;
and Rabbi Eliezer holds:
a plain large one is also for lying on.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בִּגְדוֹלָה, תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's new reading
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute is only about a plain large mat. The תנא קמא says it is for roofing, and רבי אליעזר says it is for lying.

steps.title: Why did רבי אליעזר say 'made it for lying'?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר holds that even a plain large mat is for lying, why does he speak of a mat someone 'made for lying'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then what does רבי אליעזר mean when he says 'one made it for lying'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב פפא's reading against the actual wording of רבי אליעזר. According to that reading, even a plain mat counts as made for lying, so why does he need to mention a mat made for lying?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רבי אליעזר holds that a plain large mat is also for lying. But his words in the משנה say 'if one made it for lying', which sounds like it must have been made on purpose. The גמרא asks how that wording fits a rule that covers even plain mats.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it for lying on

phrases.english: And what is 'he made it for lying' that he says?
phrases.notes: Quoting רבי אליעזר's words from the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the conclusion of step 7 against רבי אליעזר's exact wording
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading of רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If plain mats are already treated as made for lying, the phrase 'made it for lying' seems to add nothing or to imply that intent is required.

steps.title: A plain mat counts as made for lying unless made for roofing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר means that making a mat without saying what it is for also counts as making it for lying, until someone makes it for roofing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: making a mat with no stated purpose also counts as making it for lying, unless someone makes it for roofing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'made for lying' includes a plain mat made with no stated purpose. Only a mat made on purpose for roofing is valid as סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'made for lying' is not limited to a mat made on purpose for lying. The default status of any mat is 'for lying'. The only way to change that is to make it specifically for סכך.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, every mat counts as 'for lying' unless it is made specifically for סכך. The תנא קמא holds that a plain large mat counts as made for roofing.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Plain making of it is also for lying,
until one makes it for roofing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Made it for lying' sounded like it means only a mat made on purpose for lying.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Made for lying' includes a plain mat. Only a mat made specifically for roofing is valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא sorts mats by material and size
steps.stepSummary: Large mats of papyrus or bulrush are valid for סכך and small ones are not. Coarse-plaited reed mats are valid, and finely woven ones are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a mat of papyrus or of bulrush may be used as סכך if it is large, but not if it is small. A mat of reeds or of plaiting-reeds may be used as סכך if it is coarsely plaited, but not if it is finely woven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives practical rules for which mats may be used as סכך, based on what material they are made of and how they are made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea underneath is simple. A mat that people usually lie on is not valid as סכך, and a mat that people usually use for roofing is valid. Small papyrus mats and finely woven reed mats are typically made for lying, so they are invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of reed used for plaiting

steps.confusionAlert: In the reed case, 'large' (גְּדוֹלָה) does not mean the size of the mat. It means a coarse, wide weave, in contrast to a fine weave (אֲרוּגָה).

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A mat of papyrus or of bulrush,
if large, one may roof with it,
if small, one may not roof with it.
One of reeds or of plaiting-reeds,
if coarsely plaited, one may roof with it,
if finely woven, one may not roof with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on the same topic of mats as סכך
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Large papyrus or bulrush mats and coarse reed mats are valid as סכך. Small papyrus mats and finely woven reed mats are invalid.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי allows all these mats
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, quoting his father, permits both kinds of mats as סכך. רבי דוסא holds the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says in the name of his father: one may roof with both this kind and that kind. And רבי דוסא used to say the same as him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a dissenting opinion that is more lenient. It allows the mats that the first opinion called invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, these mats are not assumed to be made for lying, so they may be used as סכך. רבי דוסא is named as agreeing. That detail matters, because the next step quotes a ruling of רבי דוסא about mats.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his father
Like his words, agreeing with him

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei says in the name of his father:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ מְסַכְּכִין בָּהּ.
phrases.english: With both this one and that one, one may roof.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרָיו.
phrases.english: And so Rabbi Dosa would say, in accordance with his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All these mats are valid as סכך. רבי דוסא agrees.
steps.whyThisMatters: Naming רבי דוסא here prepares the comparison with his ruling on the טומאה of mats in the next step.

steps.title: A משנה on the טומאה of mats
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא says all mats can become impure through contact with a corpse. The חכמים say they can become impure through מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: all חוצלות can become impure with טמא מת. These are the words of רבי דוסא. The חכמים say: they become impure with מדרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה from another place where רבי דוסא rules about mats. This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to compare this ruling with what רבי דוסא said about סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא treats these mats as vessels that can become impure through a corpse. The חכמים answer with מדרס, an impurity that applies only to items made for lying or sitting, so they treat these mats as made for lying. The next step questions the חכמים' wording: it sounds like they mean מדרס only, and not corpse impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
A disputed term: actual mats (ריש לקיש) or shepherds' sacks (רב אבדימי בר המדורי, as explained by רבי אבא); see steps 15-19
Impurity from a זב treading, sitting, or lying on an object made for that purpose

phrases.english: We learned there:
All חוצלות become impure with corpse impurity,
these are the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say: impurity of treading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel source involving רבי דוסא in order to compare it with step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא: mats can become impure with טמא מת. חכמים: mats can become impure with מדרס.

steps.title: Can something get מדרס impurity but not corpse impurity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the חכמים. They seem to say mats get only מדרס impurity, but a משנה teaches that anything that can get מדרס impurity can also get טמא מת impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do they really mean מדרס impurity yes, but corpse impurity no? We learned in a משנה that anything that becomes impure by מדרס also becomes impure by a corpse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with what the חכמים said in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא said mats become impure through a corpse. The חכמים answered 'through מדרס,' which sounds like 'only מדרס, not a corpse.' But a משנה says that whatever can get the stricter מדרס impurity can surely get corpse impurity, so the חכמים cannot mean 'corpse impurity, no.'

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity a זב passes to an item made for sitting or lying when he sits, lies, or leans on it
Impurity that comes from contact with a dead body
But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think מדרס is a weaker impurity than טמא מת. Only items made for sitting or lying can get מדרס, so it is the more limited category. Every item that can get מדרס can also get corpse impurity, but not every item that can get corpse impurity can get מדרס.

phrases.english: Treading impurity, yes; corpse impurity, no?
phrases.notes: This takes what the חכמים said in step 12 to mean mats only get מדרס impurity, nothing else.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
Anything that becomes impure by treading
phrases.notes: A general rule taught in a משנה.

phrases.english: becomes impure with corpse impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְרָס אִין, טְמֵא מֵת לָא? וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the חכמים' statement in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' statement that mats become impure through מדרס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The statement implies mats get מדרס but not corpse impurity. That contradicts the משנה's rule that whatever gets מדרס also gets corpse impurity.

steps.title: Read the חכמים as saying 'even מדרס'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes how we read the חכמים' words. They mean mats get corpse impurity and also מדרס impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: mats become impure even through מדרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adjusting how we read the חכמים' words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים agree with רבי דוסא that mats get corpse impurity. They add that mats also get מדרס impurity, because mats are made for lying on. So the real dispute is only about מדרס, and the משנה's rule is kept.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (a correction or rereading of a text)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי דוסא says mats get only corpse impurity. The חכמים say mats get corpse impurity and even מדרס.

phrases.english: Say: even treading impurity.
phrases.notes: Mats get corpse impurity, and also מדרס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים meant mats get only מדרס and not corpse impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים hold that mats get corpse impurity and also מדרס. This fits the משנה.

steps.title: What does the word חוצלות mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the term חוצלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are חוצלות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to define an unclear word. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before it can apply the law, the גמרא needs to know what object the word refers to. It is not yet clear whether חוצלות are mats or something else.

keyTerms.meaning: An unclear term for some woven or plaited object; its meaning is being defined here

phrases.english: What are 'chotzalot'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the impurity dispute to defining a term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word חוצלות

steps.title: רב אבדימי בר המדורי: they are מרזובלי
steps.stepSummary: רב אבדימי בר המדורי explains חוצלות as מרזובלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אבדימי בר המדורי said: they are מרזובלי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אבדימי בר המדורי answers with another word, which is itself unfamiliar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer defines one unclear word with another unclear word. That leads straight to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A local term for some kind of sack (explained in the next steps)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַבְדִּימִי בַּר הַמְדּוּרֵי: מַרְזוֹבְלֵי.
phrases.english: Rav Avdimi bar Hamduri said: 'marzovelei.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.

steps.title: What does מרזובלי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word מרזובלי means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are מרזובלי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not know the word מרזובלי either, so it asks again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer did not settle anything, because its word was also unclear. The גמרא wants a familiar term.

phrases.english: What are 'marzovelei'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word given in step 16.

steps.title: רבי אבא: they are מזבלי, shepherds' sacks
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says מרזובלי are מזבלי, which are sacks shepherds use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: they are מזבלי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives the familiar name: מזבלי, sacks used by shepherds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are sacks shepherds use to feed their animals. Shepherds also put them under their heads when they lie down. On this view, the word חוצלות does not mean ordinary mats.

keyTerms.meaning: Shepherds' sacks for animal feed, also used as pillows

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: 'mezablei.'
phrases.notes: Shepherds' feed sacks, which they rest their heads on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: חוצלות are real mats
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש disagrees and says חוצלות are actual mats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: they are actual mats.
steps.whatsHappening: A second view is given. חוצלות are not sacks but plain, real mats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, the dispute between רבי דוסא and the חכמים is about ordinary mats, not shepherds' sacks. That makes the dispute more directly connected to mats used as סכך.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
Actual mats.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: מַחְצָלוֹת מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 15's question.

steps.title: ריש לקיש is consistent: his praise of רבי חייא and his sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says ריש לקיש is following his own known view. It introduces his source with his praise of רבי חייא and his sons, who restored forgotten Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש follows his own reasoning. ריש לקיש said: I am an atonement for רבי חייא and his sons. When the Torah was first forgotten from Israel, עזרא came up from Babylonia and restored it. It was forgotten again, and הלל הבבלי came up and restored it. It was forgotten again, and רבי חייא and his sons came up and restored it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof that ריש לקיש is consistent. First it quotes his high praise of רבי חייא and his sons, whose teaching comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I am an atonement for them' is a strong way of showing love and respect. ריש לקיש places רבי חייא and his sons in the line of עזרא and הלל, who restored Torah when it was forgotten. This praise shows why he relies on their tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (he is consistent with another statement of his)
I am an atonement for (an expression of deep love and respect)

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish follows his own reasoning.
As Reish Lakish said:
I am an atonement for Rabbi Chiya and his sons,
for at first, when Torah was forgotten from Israel,
Ezra came up from Babylonia and re-established it.
It was forgotten again,
Hillel the Babylonian came up and re-established it.
It was forgotten again,
Rabbi Chiya and his sons came up and re-established it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins showing that ריש לקיש's definition in step 19 fits another of his statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש praises רבי חייא and his sons as restorers of forgotten Torah, as an introduction to their teaching.

steps.title: רבי חייא's tradition: no dispute about the mats of אושא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש quotes רבי חייא and his sons: רבי דוסא and the חכמים did not argue about the mats of אושא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רבי חייא and his sons: רבי דוסא and the חכמים did not disagree about the mats of אושא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the teaching ריש לקיש cites from רבי חייא and his sons. The sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition speaks of the dispute between רבי דוסא and the חכמים as being about מחצלות, which are mats. That matches ריש לקיש's view that חוצלות means real mats. It also says there is one kind of mat, from אושא, that they did not argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: אושא, a town in the Galilee known for a certain kind of mat

steps.whyThisMatters: This tradition is the basis for saying ריש לקיש is consistent. The dispute in step 12 is about actual mats, with the mats of אושא as an exception the גמרא explains on the next amud.

phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Chiya and his sons:
Rabbi Dosa and the Sages did not disagree
about the mats of Usha
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual teaching that the praise in step 20 introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא and the חכמים did not disagree about the mats of אושא (continued on the next amud).
